claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is prepared by conventional atomization.
The feedstock has morphology and composition typical of powders used for miniature-component fabrication.
Active localized cryogenic interlayer cooling can be integrated into the additive-manufacturing process.
In-situ cryogenic cooling will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
In-situ cryogenic cooling will improve mechanical properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The proposed processing window applies to miniature components with dimensions on the order of centimeters.
Localized cryogenic cooling can be applied effectively at the stated centimeter-scale geometry.
Cryogenic interlayer cooling reduces the thermal gradient during layer deposition.
Reducing the deposition thermal gradient alleviates the formation of high residual stresses.
Cryogenic interlayer cooling promotes a more uniform microstructure.
Cryogenic interlayer cooling reduces the tendency for crack formation.
High thermal gradients cause rapid local solidification and the buildup of thermal stresses.
Removing heat immediately after deposition minimizes high thermal gradients.
The cooling intervention promotes a refined and homogenized microstructure.
A refined and homogenized microstructure produces improved mechanical properties.
Cooled components will have fewer microstructural defects, including less cracking, than baseline components.
Cooled components will have higher tensile strength than baseline components.
Cooled components will have higher ductility than baseline components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing produces higher residual stresses and degraded mechanical properties.
Nonuniform cooling and thermal shock may limit the outcomes of the intervention.
